facts.value: on or before the date the wages would have been paid had employment continued
facts.summary: Virginia: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due on or before the date the wages would have been paid had employment continued.
facts.evidence_quote: Upon termination of employment an employee shall be paid all wages due him for work performed prior thereto; such payment shall be made on or before the date on which he would have been paid for such work had his employment not been terminated.
facts.source_title: Code of Virginia 40.1-29, Time and medium of payment

facts.value: on or before the date the wages would have been paid had employment continued
facts.summary: Virginia: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on or before the date the wages would have been paid had employment continued.
facts.evidence_quote: Upon termination of employment an employee shall be paid all wages due him for work performed prior thereto; such payment shall be made on or before the date on which he would have been paid for such work had his employment not been terminated.
facts.source_title: Code of Virginia 40.1-29, Time and medium of payment
facts.notes: Statute says 'termination of employment' without distinguishing quit from discharge.

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Virginia basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $12.77.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $12.77 The Virginia minimum wage is adjusted annually based on a set formula.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)

facts.value: All employers with business operations in the State of Virginia are required to report all newly hired or rehired employees who live or work in Virginia within twenty (20) days of the employees’ first day on the job. State and federal laws require employers to report paid individuals regardless of whether the individuals are considered employees by federal tax code standards. § 63.2- 1946. law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title63.2 /chapter19/section63.2-1946/
facts.summary: Virginia new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): All employers with business operations in the State of Virginia are required to report all newly hired or rehired employees who live or work in Virginia within twenty (20) days of the employees’ first day on the job. State and federal laws require employers to report paid individuals regardless of whether the individuals are considered employees by federal tax code standards. § 63.2- 1946. law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title63.2 /chapter19/section63.2-1946/
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: All employers with business operations in the State of Virginia are required to report all newly hired or rehired employees who live or work in Virginia within twenty (20) days of the employees’ first day on the job. State and federal laws require employers to report paid individuals regardless of whether the individuals are considered employees by federal tax code standards. § 63.2- 1946. law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title63.2 /chapter19/section63.2-1946/
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)

facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Virginia: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Weekly (note 24); Bi-weekly (note 24); Semi-monthly (note 24); Monthly (note 2).
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 2: Illinois, Nevada, New Mexico, and Virginia. Monthly payday requirements for Executive, Administrative, and Professional personnel. | Note 24: Virginia. Employees whose weekly wages total more than 150 percent of the average weekly wage of the Commonwealth may be paid monthly, upon agreement of each affected employee. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.value: Salaried employees at least monthly; hourly employees at least every two weeks or twice a month
facts.summary: Virginia pay frequency rule: Salaried employees at least monthly; hourly employees at least every two weeks or twice a month.
facts.evidence_quote: All such employers shall pay salaried employees at least once each month and employees paid on an hourly rate at least once every two weeks or twice in each month
facts.notes: Exceptions for work-study students and employees above 150% of the state average weekly wage who agree to monthly pay.

facts.summary: Virginia is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
